text:
Josh Morrissey played 25 minutes and 30 seconds on Thursday, more than anyone on the ice, and the last shift was the one that counted. At 1:58 of overtime he beat Semyon Varlamov with a wrist shot, set up by Mark Scheifele and Kyle Connor, and Winnipeg had a 4-3 win at Canada Life Centre. It ended the Islanders' three-game winning streak and gave the Jets a bounce back two nights after Ottawa snapped their six-game run.

The first 21 minutes were a trading session. Anthony Duclair scored at 2:35, Morgan Barron tipped one in 31 seconds later, and Emil Heineman put New York ahead again shorthanded on a shot our numbers gave a 2% chance. Connor tied it late in the first, Kyle Palmieri scored 20 seconds into the second, and Cole Perfetti answered on the power play at 12:09. That Perfetti goal moved Winnipeg's win chance from 33% to 54%, and nobody scored again until overtime.

Scheifele had three assists, the latest line in a month where headlines keep calling him a record breaker, and his top unit with Connor and Gabriel Vilardi drove the night. Winnipeg finished with 3.44 expected goals (the quality of their chances, not just the count) to New York's 2.73, and won 62% of our replays of every shot. The Islanders took more attempts, 60 to 49, but the Jets got the better looks, including two power plays worth 1.06 expected goals.

In goal, this is still a strange season in Winnipeg. With Connor Hellebuyck traded to New Jersey in October, Nico Daws got the start and made 22 saves on 25 shots. His biggest came in the second period on Casey Cizikas, the best chance of the night that didn't go in. Varlamov stopped 18 of 22 and still earned the third star.

For the Islanders, the worry is off the scoresheet. Pete DeBoer had no update on Ryan Pulock afterward and said he will have to see doctors, according to Stefen Rosner of NHL.com. A point on the road is fine. A long Pulock absence would not be.
headline: Morrissey ends it, and the Islanders' run with it
